content:
pagerduty-bot: Incident triggered: high tail-latency and token-queue growth on production inference pool (region: us-west-2). Pager: @sharon, @ming

sharon: I'm on it. seeing a spike in `prefix-kv` memory usage in the MQA Qwen deployment. tails up to 3.2s for a subset of requests.

ming: noticed correlation with continuous-batching rollout (cfg v2.4). MQA requests expanding KV entries per request (token-splitting) — cache entries exploding.

ryan: any customer-facing errors?

sharon: no 5xxs yet but elevated timeouts on some routes; a major client reported degraded interactive latency. they saw typing lag.

oncall-amber: I'm taking pager for the next shift at 22:00 PT. handing off after we stabilize.

infra-bot: Deploy vm-ops:autoscales disabled on pool kv-prefix-1 by @sharon.

samir: quick triage: metrics show average KV entry size increasing ~6x for MQA requests; eviction isn't keeping up because continuous-batching keeps appending partial KV entries. looks like a GQA vs MQA mismatch — some backends expect GQA framing and produce larger prefixes.

alex: can we throttle continuous batching temporarily? a safe hotfix is to disable continuous-batching for MQA models and force eviction pressure.

sharon: doing that now. patching pool config to set `continuous_batching=false` for model_group=qwen-mqa.

sharon: command I ran:```bash
redwoodctl pools update kv-prefix-1 --set continuous_batching=false --selector model_group=qwen-mqa
```

ming: also set eviction to aggressive LRU for 10min:```bash
redwoodctl runtime update --pool kv-prefix-1 --set eviction.policy=lru --set eviction.target_entries=250000
```

samir: pushing a canary change to reduce max_batch_tokens to 512 for MQA so we don't split into many small kv fragments.

ryan: rolling canary to 3 hosts now. watch RPS and tail p50/p95.

infra-bot: Canary rollout started: kv-prefix-1/canary-3 (hosts: i-0a3e, i-0b4f, i-0c5d).

oncall-amber: noted. alerting support that we're investigating latency; CS notified that we're rolling a fix.

sharon: immediate effect: KV growth stopped on canary hosts. tail p95 dropped from 3.2s -> 0.9s on those hosts.

ming: fetching logs to confirm root cause. grep shows repeated small partial sequences being written as separate KV frames:```
[INFO] write_kv: key=ctx:abc123:seg:1 len=2048
[INFO] write_kv: key=ctx:abc123:seg:2 len=1900
[INFO] write_kv: key=ctx:abc123:seg:3 len=2056
```

samir: those lengths look like MQA split logic creating many fragments for GQA-mode model copies. looks like the MQA/generation policy didn't map to the model variant properly after last rolling deploy.

alex: do we have matching model variant tags? maybe a mismatch in `variant_suffix` between runtime and model catalog.

sharon: found a config drift: qwen-mqa variant mistakenly pointed to a qwen-gqa-compat image (v1.8) after last canary. that image uses older token framing.

ryan: ok root cause identified. plan: 1) keep continuous-batching disabled for qwen-mqa 2) revert variant pointer to v1.9-mqa on production 3) aggressive eviction until pools stabilize 4) run regression tests for MQA/GQA interop.

oncall-amber: I'll own the redeploy and post-deploy smoke. taking over live monitor for the next 2hrs.

infra-bot: Rolling update: model-catalog/qwen-mqa -> image v1.9-mqa by @oncall-amber.

sharon: rolling now. brief expected churn per host ~30s, will stagger across AZs.

ming: also patching batcher to conserve KV keys: set `max_consecutive_fragments=4` for temporary mitigation.

sharon: revert is done on canary hosts, now promoting to remaining pool. watching evictions and memory.

infra-bot: Update complete: 12/12 hosts updated.

ryan: metrics: p95 back to 0.8s cluster-wide, KV store mem usage trending down to normal.

samir: double-checking edge cases: GQA clients hitting MQA endpoints could still produce mismatched frames; need to add a runtime sanity check to reject mismatched frame formats and log with high priority.

alex: agree — add a temporary guard: if `fragment_count > 8` then coalesce and mark request for postmortem.

sharon: added guard in runtime gate and deployed to canary. will instrument to slice by model and client.

oncall-amber: CS update drafted: "We've mitigated a performance regression affecting some Qwen MQA flows by rolling back a model variant and adjusting batching config. If you continue to see issues, please open a ticket." sending now.

samir: creating incident postmortem ticket with hypothesis and timeline. assign to infra and runtime.

sharon: handing off to @oncall-amber for night - full rundown sent to the rotations channel.

oncall-amber: taking over. I have runbooks and the hotfix steps noted. will keep monitoring until 02:00 PT, will page if regressions recur.

ryan: great work all. follow-ups: - make variant pointer checks part of canary gating - add KV-fragment coalescing in next runtime release - add e2e test covering GQA vs MQA frame compatibility

pagerduty-bot: Incident resolved: mitigation applied and verified. Severity downgraded to S3. Incident channel will remain open for postmortem notes. :tada:

sharon: adding a few logs/screenshots to the postmortem doc after I scrub PII and client ids.

samir: thanks. closing loop once postmortem published.

alex: nice fast loop. :thumbsup:
